summary: Jeremiah calls mourners to put on sackcloth and roll in ashes. The Peshitta uses a similarly spelled verb for thieves breaking through a house. Philistia and Philistine are also filed here, but the origin of the people’s name is uncertain.

senses.definition: A member of the people whose rulers governed Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron. The singular identifies Goliath of Gath and the plural names the people collectively.

evidence.note: The five cities supply one offering apiece on behalf of the Philistines.

senses.definition: The territory inhabited by the Philistines. Prophets can address the land as a whole or distinguish its several districts.

evidence.note: Joel addresses all the regions of Philistia alongside Tyre and Sidon.

senses.definition: A member of a body of royal retainers repeatedly named with the Cherethites.

evidence.note: The groups pass before David as he leaves Jerusalem.

words.summary: Their service to David is clear. The shorter name has been compared with “Philistine,” but the passages do not establish that derivation.

senses.definition: A mourner lowers himself into dust or ashes, accompanying bitter cries or the wearing of sackcloth.

evidence.note: Those mourning Tyre cast dust on their heads and roll in ashes.

senses.definition: Thieves force an opening to reach property stored inside.

evidence.note: Breaking in precedes stealing in the warning about laying up treasure.

senses.definition: A house is breached while its owner is unprepared.

evidence.note: Keeping watch would have prevented the house from being broken into.

note: The Ugaritic text ties wallowing to mourning and preserves ṯ. The Akkadian and Syriac verbs of breaking in provide a separate comparison. No verse derives the people’s name from a verb meaning to invade. The three indexed Hithpael tokens omit the spelling in Mic 1:10. The conjunction פֶּן and the foodstuff פַּנַּג have different consonants and no demonstrated derivation from פלש. Peleth is the name of two people (Num 16:1 and 1Ch 2:33); the name itself has no shin and no demonstrated link to this root. No personal name file assigned.
